_about: COOKROLES: spec 08 §2-4. Ingredient ROLES for a cooking recipe's slots and the inheritance rules that say which of an ingredient INSTANCE's traits, processing history and flags reach the finished dish. Read by scripts/items/cook_roles.gd. A slot names a role (main, topping, sauce, broth, spice, support); the role narrows the item categories a slot accepts, so a spice can never fill the main slot. Inheritance is per slot and per recipe: a recipe must set "inherit": true, and every slot's own "inherit" block decides what passes from THAT exact instance (no averaging, no stacking: the first slot that carries a key in slot order wins). A recipe or slot without a role keeps the old category-only behaviour, so every earlier recipe is untouched.

provenance._about: Which role names and rules come from a source and which are this build's own placeholder (spec 08 §3/§10: the reconstructed inheritance tables are partly estimated, never present them as 2019 server constants).
provenance.source: spec 08 §3: slots named main/topping/sauce/broth/spice/support; only qualifying main slots transfer cooking properties; toppings/sauces/broth can add their own recipe-defined bonuses; rare traits pass only through a recipe-defined conversion.
provenance.assumption: The category lists, the default inheritance flags, the trait effect amounts and the buff rows are # ASSUMPTION placeholders. Retune here, in data only.

main._about: Spec 08 §3: the main ingredient is what may carry existing cooking properties. # ASSUMPTION: water and drink are deliberately not main categories (they fill a broth/sauce slot), nor is spice or herb.

topping._about: Spec 08 §3/§4: a topping adds its own recipe-defined bonus even when it inherits nothing.

sauce._about: Spec 08 §3: a sauce can add a bonus. # ASSUMPTION: juice/drink stand in until sauce items exist.

broth._about: Spec 08 §3/§4: broth carries the dish's liquid. The attribute bonus a documented bone/meat/fish/vegetable broth gives belongs to the broth item's own food (foods.json); a plain water broth grants none yet, because no bone/fish broth item exists in items.json.

spice._about: Spec 08 §3: seasoning. Narrow on purpose: only items with the spice category.

support._about: Spec 08 §3's catch-all (a skewer's stick, a pot, fuel): accepts anything the slot's own category allows and inherits nothing.

inherit._about: Default inheritance flags per role, overridden per recipe slot by the slot's own "inherit" block. traits: true = every non-rare instance trait, false = none, or a list of exact trait keys. processed = the instance's in-place cooking history (processing.json), which is what carries drying/smoking cooking properties. flags = the instance's flags. rare = the green/rare material attributes (rules.json crafting.rare_attributes) may pass.

trait_effects._about: What an INHERITED food trait does to the dish's FOODFX bundle (scripts/items/food_effects.gd). Only a dish that recorded the trait through inheritance (attributes.cooked_roles) gets these; a raw ingredient carrying the same attribute is unaffected. Rows use FOODFX's field/op/value shape; per_level scales the value by the trait's level on the instance. # ASSUMPTION: the keys, channels and amounts - spec 08 §3/§4 list the kinds of effect, not their numbers.

rich_cut._about: A fattier cut: more Energy and a little more Fullness per trait level.

gamey_cut._about: Strong meat fills more and leaves a thirst.

fresh_cut._about: Spec 08 §4 lists Health as a food benefit; a fresh cut adds a little.

role_bonus._about: Spec 08 §3: toppings, sauces and broth add their own recipe-defined bonus even when they do not inherit. Keyed by role, then by an item category the ingredient has (the first match in the role's category order wins); the bonus is a buff id from this file's buffs block. # ASSUMPTION: which category grants which buff. Spec 08 §4 names bell pepper/grape/tomato/pumpkin/onion toppings and fruit dishes; those items are not in items.json yet, so the bonus is keyed by category and shown per dish.

buffs._about: The buffs a role bonus grants, in FOODFX's buff-bundle shape (group, display_name, duration, stats). The group is comments.json buff_groups 'cooked_role' (COOKROLES): a topping's own bonus is its own category, so it neither replaces nor is replaced by the dish's signature Enhanced Ability/Survival buff, and the newest role bonus replaces the last. # ASSUMPTION: 10 min and the stat amounts (spec 08 §4 gives one community figure, ~+4 ability, and calls it unconfirmed).
